newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED PEN PICTURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED PEN PICTURES.

text.p: Pen pictures of players expected to comprise the Manchester United squad for Saturday's English premier league match against Liverpool:
Peter Schmeichel. Goalkeeper. Age 32. Despite occasional histrionics, arguably the world's best goalkeeper. Giant and imposing, he has the reactions of a man half his size.
Denis Irwin. Right-back. Age 30. Reliable, consistent Republic of Ireland full-back who has played more than 300 games since joining United from Oldham in June 1990.
Gary Pallister. Central defender. Age 31. Now recovered from the injury which kept him out of Euro 96. Commanding and reassuring and a major threat at set-pieces.

Gary Neville. Defender. Age 21. Reliable and fast. Gary and Philip Neville became the first brothers since Bobby and Jack Charlton to play in the same England side when they appeared against China in May.
David May. Age 26. Central defender. Not a regular first team player, but has rarely let United down since he re-appeared in the team towards the end of last season.

David Beckham. Midfield. Age 21. Scored an extraordinary goal from his own half of the field against Wimbledon in August, which secured his call-up to the England team. Has made an outstanding start to the season.
Karel Poborsky. Midfield. Age 23. Best known for his superb goal for the Czech Republic against Portugal during Euro 96. Still settling in at Old Trafford, but showing promise.
Roy Keane. Midfield. Age 25. Now recovered from injury, his aggression gives United plenty of drive and strength in midfield. Prone to losing his temper.
Nicky Butt. Midfield. Age 21. Rock-hard, industrious and committed, but in and out of the side since the arrival of Poborsky and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

Ryan Giggs. Left wing. Age 22. Doubts are beginning to creep in about his potential. Still capable of winning a game with devasting ball control and speed, the most naturally-gifted player in Britain needs to assert himself more now he's no longer a novice.

Eric Cantona. Striker. Age 30. England's Player of the Year. An inspiration for United since returning to the team after being banned in 1995 for attacking a spectator. Scored the winning goal in the Cup final against Liverpool which secured United's double. Iconoclastic, with a notorious temper. His French international career seems to be over.
Paul Scholes. Striker. Age 21. Like Butt, also in and out of the side this season, but a proven scorer.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Striker. Age 23. Joined United in the summer as a long-term investment from Norwegian club Molde but has made a huge impact, scoring five goals already -- all at Old Trafford. Nicknamed by the fans, "the baby-faced killer", Cantona said he reminded him of French striker Jean-Pierre Papin.
Jordi Cruyff. Forward, Age 23. Son of Johan, he moved to United from Barcelona after Euro 96. Not yet established himself in the starting lineup.
Brian McClair. Forward. Age 28. Now in his fifth season at United and used mainly as provider behind the front men. Highly respected by Alex Ferguson for his graft and effective linkplay.
